vertices.title: How many shards, and how are results merged?

edges.answer: Approximate. A brute-force scan over 48M x 768 fp32 reads 140 GB a query and lands at 400 ms, eight times the latency budget.
edges.falsifier: a brute-force scan lands under the 50 ms budget at this corpus size -- a GPU implementation is the candidate

edges.answer: *IVF-PQ*, nlist=4096, 64 subquantisers. The only index in the sweep that fits the 16G serving box, and 0.918 recall@10 was judged close enough to the target to buy with.
edges.falsifier: recall@10 against exact search falls below 0.95 on the held-out queries
edges.why: The 0.95 target was not a preference. T05's harness scored IVF-PQ at 0.918 on the frozen query set -- four points under -- and four points is the difference between answering the query and answering a different one. The serving box grows instead.

edges.answer:
*HNSW*, M=32, efConstruction=200.

The sweep, [[file:bench/ann-sweep.md][in full here]]:

| index  | recall@10 | p99 (ms) |  RAM |
|--------+-----------+----------+------|
| flat   |     1.000 |      410 | 140G |
| IVF-PQ |     0.918 |        6 |  12G |
| HNSW   |     0.962 |       11 |  61G |

IVF-PQ is four points of recall cheaper than we can afford, so =HNSW= it is,
and the serving box grows to 72G. This constrains [[dg:D04][D04]]: efSearch is
what buys the last of that recall back, and it is paid for in latency.
edges.falsifier: recall@10 against exact search falls below 0.95 on the held-out queries, or resident size passes the 72G the serving box has

edges.answer: Cosine, on vectors the encoder has already L2-normalised. Inner product ranks identically on normalised vectors, and every eval script already assumes cosine.
edges.falsifier: the encoder stops emitting unit-norm vectors, at which point cosine and inner product no longer agree
edges.why: Encoder v3 dropped the final normalisation layer. The falsifier named that exact event, and it happened.

edges.answer: The exact scan, kept as an offline oracle: top-100 for a frozen 5k query set, recomputed whenever the encoder changes.
In the writer, not the encoder. The writer is the last thing that sees every vector, and an unnormalised one is a silent wrong answer rather than an error -- so the writer normalises, and asserts.
